DZA.summary: Between the Mediterranean coast and the Sahara.
DZA.borderNote: Also borders Western Sahara, shown separately as disputed territory.

AGO.summary: Cabinda is separated from the main part of Angola.

BEN.summary: A narrow coastal country between Togo and Nigeria.

BWA.summary: Between Namibia, Zimbabwe and South Africa, with a short Zambia border.

BFA.summary: An inland meeting point for six West African neighbors.

BDI.summary: South of Rwanda, beside Lake Tanganyika.

CPV.summary: An Atlantic island group west of Senegal.

CMR.summary: Stretches from the Gulf of Guinea toward Lake Chad.

CAF.summary: An inland link between the two Congos and Sudan.

TCD.summary: Extends north from Lake Chad into the Sahara.

COD.summary: The larger Congo has a narrow outlet to the Atlantic.

COG.summary: West of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

CIV.summary: On the Gulf of Guinea between Liberia and Ghana.

DJI.summary: At the narrow entrance between the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden.
DJI.borderNote: The Somalia boundary meets Somaliland, shown separately as a disputed / breakaway area.

EGY.summary: The Nile reaches the Mediterranean here; Sinai extends into Asia.
EGY.borderNote: Also borders Israel and the Gaza Strip (State of Palestine), outside this Africa set.

GNQ.summary: Combines a mainland section with islands in the Gulf of Guinea.

ERI.summary: A long Red Sea coast north of Ethiopia.

SWZ.summary: Between South Africa and Mozambique, without a coastline.

ETH.summary: Inland in the Horn of Africa, west of Somalia.
ETH.borderNote: Part of the Somalia boundary meets Somaliland. The map distinguishes its disputed / breakaway status.

GAB.summary: On the Atlantic coast, south of Cameroon.

GMB.summary: Follows the Gambia River through Senegal to the Atlantic.

GHA.summary: On the Gulf of Guinea, just west of Togo.

GIN.summary: An Atlantic country reaching inland toward Mali.

GNB.summary: A small Atlantic country between Senegal and Guinea.

KEN.summary: Connects the Indian Ocean coast with Lake Victoria.

LBR.summary: On the Atlantic coast between Sierra Leone and Côte d’Ivoire.

LBY.summary: Mediterranean coastline above a broad Saharan interior.

MDG.summary: A large island across the Mozambique Channel from mainland Africa.

MWI.summary: A narrow inland country along Lake Malawi.

MLI.summary: Links the western Sahel with the Sahara.

MRT.summary: Atlantic coastline beside the western Sahara.
MRT.borderNote: Also borders Western Sahara, shown separately as disputed territory.

MUS.summary: An Indian Ocean island country east of Madagascar.

MAR.summary: At Africa’s northwest corner, across the strait from Spain.
MAR.borderNote: Also meets Spain at Ceuta and Melilla. Western Sahara is shown separately as disputed territory.

MOZ.summary: Its long Indian Ocean coast faces Madagascar.

NAM.summary: Its northeastern arm reaches toward Zambia.

NER.summary: Inland north of Nigeria; the similar names describe different countries.

NGA.summary: On the Gulf of Guinea, south of Niger.

RWA.summary: A small inland country between Uganda and Burundi.

STP.summary: Two main islands in the Gulf of Guinea, west of Gabon.

SEN.summary: Surrounds The Gambia except at its Atlantic mouth.

SYC.summary: An Indian Ocean archipelago northeast of Madagascar.

SLE.summary: On the Atlantic coast between Guinea and Liberia.

SOM.summary: Forms the eastern tip of the Horn of Africa.
SOM.borderNote: Somaliland is shown separately as a disputed / breakaway area, not a 55th sovereign country.

ZAF.summary: Wraps around Lesotho at the continent’s southern end.

SSD.summary: Inland between Sudan and the Great Lakes region.
SSD.borderNote: The boundary with Sudan includes unresolved disputes, including Abyei.

SDN.summary: South of Egypt, with a short Red Sea coast.
SDN.borderNote: Some boundaries and areas, including Abyei, remain disputed.

TZA.summary: Links the Great Lakes to the Indian Ocean.

TGO.summary: A slender strip between Ghana and Benin.

TUN.summary: A Mediterranean country between Algeria and Libya.

UGA.summary: An inland country on the northern side of Lake Victoria.

ZMB.summary: An inland crossroads with eight neighboring countries.

ZWE.summary: Between Zambia and South Africa, west of Mozambique.

history.name: Upper Volta
history.note: The independent state changed its name to Burkina Faso.

history.name: Republic of Dahomey
history.note: Renamed Benin in 1975; this entry refers to the modern republic, not the earlier kingdom.

history.name: Swaziland
history.note: The country adopted the name Eswatini.

history.name: Zaire
history.note: The state became the Democratic Republic of the Congo; it is distinct from the Republic of the Congo.

history.name: Cape Verde
history.note: The country requested Cabo Verde for international usage; this was a name change, not a new state.

history.name: Gold Coast
history.note: A colonial-era name associated with the territory that became Ghana; not a separate former sovereign country.

history.name: Northern Rhodesia
history.note: The British-administered territory became independent Zambia.

history.name: Southern Rhodesia / Rhodesia
history.note: The minority government’s unilateral Rhodesian state lacked international recognition; Zimbabwe became independent in 1980.

history.name: Bechuanaland Protectorate
history.note: The protectorate became Botswana; this is not the same territory as British Bechuanaland, now in South Africa.

history.name: Tanganyika and Zanzibar
history.note: The two states united; the name Tanzania followed later in 1964. Zanzibar remains a distinct part of the union.

history.name: Mali Federation
history.note: Senegal withdrew from the federation; the remaining Soudanese Republic took the name Mali in September 1960.

history.name: Sudan before South Sudan’s independence
history.note: South Sudan separated from Sudan; Sudan continued as a state, and some boundary issues remain unresolved.

history.name: United Arab Republic
history.note: Egypt and Syria united, then separated. Egypt retained the union’s name until 1971; Syria is outside this map.

history.name: South West Africa
history.note: The territory became Namibia after South African rule; its status and occupation were internationally contested.

history.name: Ethiopia before Eritrean independence
history.note: Eritrea became independent; Ethiopia continued as a state and no longer had a coastline.
